sections.heading: C — Graduated licensing and license records
sections.markdown:
## C — Graduated licensing and license records

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Montana’s graduated licensing program gives new drivers under 18 an instruction permit, then a first-year restricted license, then full driving privileges. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Before moving beyond the supervised permit stage, teen drivers must practice for at least 50 hours, including 10 at night, over at least six months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
Under the graduated program, a learner-permit driver must be supervised by a licensed parent, guardian or responsible adult, or a licensed adult authorized by one of them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Everyone riding with a graduated-program instruction-permit driver must wear a seatbelt. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
To advance to the restricted-license stage, a teen must have no traffic violations or alcohol-or-drug offenses during the preceding six months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A02
A teen’s learner-permit prerequisites include passing the required driver-license written test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A02
A teen seeking a learner permit must turn in any other driver licenses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A02
A teen learner-permit applicant must meet the medical requirements for the requested license type. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A02
A teen learner-permit applicant must not have a court finding of mental incompetence, alcoholism or habitual illegal-drug use. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A02
A teen may obtain a learner permit as early as age 14½ only while participating in, or after successfully completing, a state-approved traffic education program. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
Online traffic education does not satisfy the approved-course requirement for the teen learner-permit paths. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
An exam-station learner permit is available at 16 without traffic education, or at 15 after successful completion of a state-approved traffic education program. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
A teenager under 18 must hold a learner permit for at least six consecutive months before applying for the first-year restricted license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
The teen learner license is valid for up to one year. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
The exam-station application for a restricted license requires first-stage completion, fees and required paperwork, including a completed form titled Graduated Driver Licensing Parent/Legal Guardian/Responsible Adult Certification. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
The first-year restricted license displays a restriction code on its front and back. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
Everyone in the vehicle must wear a seatbelt when the teen drives on a first-year restricted license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
A restricted-license teenager must not drive from 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. except for the limited authorized purposes described in the graduated-licensing rules. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
The restricted-license night-driving exceptions include emergencies, farm activities, school, church or work travel, and specific purposes authorized by a parent, guardian or responsible adult. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
Officers may contact the teen’s parent, guardian or responsible adult to check the purpose of driving during restricted nighttime hours. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A02
During the first six months of the restricted license, a teen may carry only one unrelated passenger under 18 unless a licensed adult driver supervises. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A02
During the second six months of the restricted license, a teen may carry three unrelated passengers under 18 unless supervised by a licensed adult driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A02
A first violation of a first-year license restriction carries 20 to 60 hours of community service. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A02
A second first-year license restriction violation results in a six-month license suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A02
First-year license restrictions end automatically on the date shown on the license back or at age 18, whichever happens sooner. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A03
A driver-license receipt lasts one year and gives a testing applicant three examination attempts within that period. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A03
Driver-license receipts cannot be renewed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A03
If licensing is unfinished after one year, the applicant must apply again and restart the process. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0019]

Misconceptions: A renewal grace period does not restore driving authority to an expired license; passenger limits also depend on supervision.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: practice, restrictions, privileges; for records, check validity before driving.
Glossary: Instruction permit; first-year restricted license; full-privilege license; licensing receipt; renewal; certified decree.

sections.heading: C2 — Graduated licensing and license records
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Graduated licensing and license records

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
A driver may begin renewal up to six months before the license expiration date. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
An expired license gives no authority to drive, even during the period when renewal without retesting may still be available. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A01
Renewal without retesting may be completed within one year after expiration. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A01
A license expired for more than one year requires a new-driver application with acceptable identity, residence and authorized-presence proof and all applicable licensing tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A01
The full legal name and birth date used on a license or identification-card application must match Social Security Administration records. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A01
The handbook’s renewal procedure requires proper identification, the fee, an exam-station appearance, a vision test and a new photo. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A01
Renewal applicants whose functional ability to drive safely is in doubt may also need written and road tests. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A01
A suspension or revocation in Montana or another jurisdiction prevents applying for, receiving or retaining a Montana driver license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A02
A lost or destroyed license can be replaced at a local licensing station with proper identity evidence verifying full legal name and birth date and the required fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A02
A driver must notify the Department of Justice Driver Services Bureau within 10 days after an address change. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A02
To change the legal name on a license, an applicant must complete the appropriate application and submit an accepted legal name-change document. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A02
An issuing government jurisdiction’s certified marriage certificate is an accepted license name-change document. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A02
A certified competent-court decree or judgment granting a name change is accepted for a license name change. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A02
A certified divorce or marriage-dissolution decree qualifies for a license name change only if it specifies the requested name change. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A02
A certified DHS USCIS naturalization certificate on form N-550 or N-570 issued to the applicant qualifies as a license name-change document. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A02
The name and birth date used for a license name change must match the Social Security Administration’s records. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0020]
